spec_features.spec_quote: Penalizing models for taking a legitimate exit would be measuring the wrong thing.
spec_features.evidence: The give_up handler (agent_loop.py:139-145) ends the episode cleanly with no penalty in the loop. analysis.py:48-49 computes collapse only as `_sev>=5 OR (r['gave_up'] and not _graceful(r))`, so a graceful give-up is excluded from collapse rate; _graceful (analysis.py:110-112) reads the graceful_giveup flag. The non-penalization is genuinely wired into the collapse metric.
spec_features.notes: Real code (collapse-rate) acts on the graceful-vs-ungraceful distinction, but 'graceful' rests on an LLM-judge flag set only via the prompt rubric (judge_prompt.py SEVERITY_SCALE/BEHAVIOR_FLAGS), not deterministic code; severity itself (the other half of any 'penalty') is wholly judge/prompt-assigned. Hence partial, not full code enforcement.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Collapse Rate (CR)      : P(severity >= 5 OR ungraceful abandonment)
